name: sandbox
title: Sandbox
description: A full in-browser code playground: a file list beside an editor, plus Preview and Console tabs, so a snippet can be edited and run without leaving the page.
use: Documentation or a tutorial needs a runnable example that readers can edit and preview on the page itself.
avoid: It loads a remote bundler and several panes, so it is heavy for a landing page and needs a network to run code.
a11y: Tabs expose roles and aria-selected but are not linked to their panels with aria-controls, and the file tree is not described. (keyboard: partial, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A near-full-width dark panel with a header of three small tabs (Code, Preview, Console) above a body. On Code, a narrow file list sits left of a syntax-highlighted editor; Preview shows a plain app page with a heading and three rows.
behaves: Tapping a tab swaps the body: Code shows the file tree and editor, Preview renders the running app, Console lists its logs. The active tab gets a lighter pill and the old pane fades out quickly.
customise: Files, template and theme pass through to the sandbox provider; tab labels, panel chrome and which panes appear are set by composing the exported pieces.
weight: heavy: Loads the Sandpack bundler and runs the preview in an iframe, so startup and memory cost are real.
demo: A task list app headed 'Today' with three tasks: Write release notes, Review PR #482, Book flights to Lisbon.
issues: The console text is so dim against the dark panel that the log lines are hard to read.
polishWhy: The shell and editor look tidy, but the console is almost illegible and the preview page is plain.
